d: The American University of the Middle East (AUM) is a leading higher education institution established in 2005 in Kuwait, distinguished by its innovative curricula, integrated and environmentally friendly campus, and a culture that fosters diversity and innovation.
AUM has achieved International Quality Accreditation (IQA) from the Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA), UK, in addition to international accreditations for its academic programs.

AUM is ranked #1 in Kuwait in both the 2027 QS World and Arab Region University Rankings, securing #616 globally and #22 in the Arab region, placing it among the top 650 universities worldwide and the top 30 universities in the Arab world.

The College of Engineering and Technology (CoET) at AUM is dedicated to maintaining high quality academic programs by adopting a learner centered approach. CoET aspires to prepare students for life-long learning and careers in engineering for engineering students, and in technology for technology students; with emphasis on leadership skills and creative work so they can lead cultural, social, and economic development.
The College of Engineering and Technology (CoET) at AUM is recruiting full-time faculty members with Master’s or PHD in the following majors:
q: A Master’s or PHD from an internationally accredited university.
Have a solid commitment to teaching excellence and student advising at undergraduate level.
Prepare teaching materials, maintain and improve competence in subjects being taught.
Ability to work in a diverse, interdisciplinary, and fast-paced environment is essential.
Have demonstrable skills in oral and written English.
Industry experience is a plus for this position.

d: UMO is a stealth-mode FinTech venture aiming to evolve the way people experience money by building a unified, AI-powered, yet deeply human money platform across fiat, crypto, and investments – subject to regulatory approvals. The platform is being designed to break down traditional barriers to money across access, assets, and experience, enabling simpler, more adaptive ways for people to interact with financial services.

We are currently developing our MVP and navigating licensing requirements, with a multidisciplinary team of 100+ people representing 20+ nationalities. With our headquarters in the UAE, we are united behind a shared ambition and a relentless focus on serving our customers.

You will own internal IT end to end — identity and access, SaaS services, workstations and the corporate network that every colleague relies on daily. You'll lead a team of five administrators and take charge of the subscription budget, quarterly planning and renewals. We give you real decision-making authority: only spend above the limit, headcount or key vendor changes, risk acceptance and company-wide changes go up for approval. Everything else is your call, within the boundaries set out under "Decision Rights".
q: Leadership: 2+ years of directly managing system administrators or IT engineers, including a distributed team. You have hired, given difficult feedback and changed priorities mid-quarter in a way the team understood.
Okta, in depth: SSO, SCIM, lifecycle management, MFA policies, Workflows. You have implemented it or significantly restructured it, not just created users.

Cloudflare, AWS, Slack, at a working level: Cloudflare Zero Trust and DNS; AWS IAM, IAM Identity Center, billing and Cost Explorer; Slack administration: apps, guests, Slack Connect. For each, you can walk us through a change you made yourself: how you tested it and what you did when something broke. Kubernetes, CI/CD and product networking are not required.

Google Workspace, Atlassian Cloud, Kandji: Administration of Google Workspace (sharing, OAuth apps, SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and Atlassian Cloud (Jira, Confluence: permissions, projects, Okta sign-in). Kandji or another MDM for macOS.

AI, advanced level: You have built an LLM-based automation that your colleagues actually used. In the interview, you will show what was built, how you evaluated errors, where you kept a human in the loop and how much time it saves. "I write prompts in ChatGPT" is not what this role needs.
Scripting and APIs: Confident in Python or similar, and able to review other people's code.
Access and audit: You have taken access reviews through to actual revocation and answered auditors' questions.
Money: You have managed SaaS renewals and can name the amount you saved and explain where it came from.
Communication: Fluent English for vendors, documentation and the team.
Can get you a few bonus points
Fintech or another regulated industry; PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001.
Terraform for Okta, Cloudflare and AWS.
Okta Identity Governance or similar, SaaS management platforms.
Dynamic Work Environment: Vibrant offices and strong local teams across Lisbon, Dubai, Kyiv, and Lviv — with openness to remote for the right fit.
Rest & Recovery: 24 days of annual leave, dedicated paid sick leave, and observance of Public Holidays to keep you at your best.
r: This is a hands-on lead role. Roughly 30% of your time goes to people, planning and alignment, and 70% to hands-on work: complex changes, incident investigation, configuration reviews, automation. You set up routine work so that it runs without you.
Lead five administrators: 1:1s, goals, feedback. Run hiring for approved positions and, when necessary, parting ways — the latter agreed with your manager.

Organize work across time zones: open incidents are handed over in writing to a specific person, and inconvenient hours are shared fairly. Three time zones cover about 13 hours of the working day, but not 24/7: you decide what truly requires a night-time or weekend response.
Every critical system has a primary administrator and a backup who knows how to restore it.

Each quarter, bring a plan: goals, owners, a support buffer and a list of what did not make the cut. Base it on feedback from engineers, recurring incidents and the renewal calendar. At the end of the quarter, show what was done, what was not and why. If urgent work comes up mid-quarter, say what moves and at what cost.
Prepare a monthly report for the area: service and support health, access status, subscription spend and optimization results, key risks and items that need a management decision.
The identity provider is the central point of access provisioning: SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, role-based groups, SCIM. Hiring, transfers and terminations are triggered from the HR system.

You verify revocation in the application itself. Deactivating a user in the identity provider does not end active sessions or revoke API tokens, local accounts and guest access. Systems without SCIM have an owner for manual revocation, and you make sure it is done.

Access review frequency depends on risk: privileged and financial systems quarterly, everything else every six months. The system owner decides on each access, revocation is confirmed in the target system, and every exception has a reason and an expiry date. Results are retained as audit evidence.

Zero Trust access and DNS: Zero Trust for internal tools (access policies, secure web gateway, device posture) and DNS for corporate domains. Policy changes roll out to a limited group first, and the on-call engineer has a rollback procedure. WAF and the product perimeter stay with DevOps.

Cloud, corporate side: Cloud SSO integrated with the identity provider, role assignments agreed with DevOps, sandbox accounts, spend in corporate accounts. Organization structure and production belong to DevOps.
Corporate messaging: Apps and integrations, guests and external channels, retention policies. Before a bot is installed, you know what data it reads and who owns it.
Collaboration suite: Mail, calendar and documents: sharing rules, third-party OAuth apps, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, data transfer at offboarding.
Ticketing and knowledge base: Permissions, projects and spaces, SSO sign-in. The ticketing system is the team's work queue, the knowledge base holds documentation.
Workstations: MDM: encryption, updates, security policies, shipping a laptop to another country with zero-touch setup.
Build self-service for developers: standard access is requested via chat or a ticket, approved by the resource owner and granted automatically for a limited time.
Set support priorities: major outages and security incidents first, then requests that block teams from working.

Together with DevOps, define clear ownership boundaries and drive shared requests to resolution: a ticket is closed when the problem is solved for the user, not when it has been handed to another team.
Maintain the SaaS registry: owner, cost, number of seats, actual usage, renewal date and the last day the order can still be changed.

Review paid seats separately from access reviews. Once a month, reconcile paid seats against activity. Long inactivity is a reason to check with the owner, not to reclaim the seat automatically: there are break-glass accounts and tools that are only needed once a quarter.

Plan each contract review backwards from the last day the order can be changed or the renewal cancelled. By that day, the volume is agreed, the negotiation position is ready and the vendor has been notified if required. Example: 80 editor seats are paid for, 30 are actively used — we go to the vendor with 35 and a question about the pricing tier.

Find shadow IT through OAuth grants and corporate card spend. In corporate cloud accounts, analyze bill growth by account and service together with the resource owner. Measure savings against invoices, separating realized savings from those expected at the next renewal.
For you, AI is the normal way the whole team works. What we expect
First-line support in chat: answers from the knowledge base with source links, request classification and ticket creation, handing unclear cases to a human.
Preparation of access reviews and license reviews: AI reconciles exports from the identity provider, the HR system and applications and produces a list of anomalies for an administrator to verify.
Measure the impact: compare time before and after rollout, including the time spent reviewing and correcting errors.

Set the rules: what data may be shared with a model and where only a human makes the decision. AI does not grant privileged access or reset MFA: an administrator does that, verifying the employee's identity before any MFA reset.
The whole team knows how to use these tools, not just you.
